definition: answers_the_ask — the output answers THIS ask, not another. The rule runs the two relevance measurements and FAILS only when BOTH fail at their thresholds: fewer than 35% of the ask's content terms appear in the output (keyword_overlap) AND fewer than a third of the output's content-bearing sentences connect to the ask, directly or through an earlier connected sentence (topic_consistency). One measurement alone never fires it. It SKIPS whenever either measurement skips — no input, an ask with no content terms, an output with fewer than six words of four or more letters — so a one-word right answer is never a fire. Critical: a fire vetoes the verdict. The labels below are a reader's: positive = the output does not address what was asked (another subject, filler, a sign-off, placeholder text); negative = it answers the ask, in whatever shape (a sentence, a list, a command, a query, one word, a hedge followed by the answer). Lexical, no model: an on-task paraphrase that reuses none of the ask's words can read as off task, and such cases are named in their notes.
source: LLM-authored on 2026-09-21 for arc 9 (N-13), from the composer probe that motivated the rule (a truncated and an off-topic answer both read clean). Twenty asks a user of this product would type, each paired with an off-task output (another subject, generic filler, a sign-off, placeholder text) and an on-task one; plus short answers the rule must decline to judge, a terse command and a query, a hedge before the answer, and one paraphrase with none of the ask's words, flagged as a possible false positive.
labelling: LLM-authored and LLM-labelled on 2026-09-21 by reading each ask and output and asking whether the output addresses what was asked — never by running the rule or either measurement. The measured gap between that reading and the lexical pair is the number published.
